name: Custom Admin URL
description: Adds a custom access check to every admin/* and user/* route that returns 403 unless the request host matches a configured back-office host, confining the administration surface to a designated URL. Defense-in-depth on top of core permissions; correctness depends on trusted host resolution.
project_description: Custom Admin URL is a small access-hardening module that confines Drupal's administration surface to a designated back-office host. On every route whose first path segment is 'admin' or 'user' it registers an extra _custom_access check (AccessController::access). When a back-office URL (a host such as back.example.com) is configured, requests to those routes coming from any other host are denied with a 403; requests from the configured host still require the core 'access administration pages' permission (with the user login route explicitly exempted). It provides one settings form at /admin/config/system/custom-admin-url storing the config object custom_admin_url.settings. It is intended as defense-in-depth alongside — not a replacement for — Drupal's role and permission system, and relies on trusted host resolution (trusted_host_patterns) so the host it keys on cannot be spoofed via the Host header.
